title: Hardcoded DTLS setup:passive in WHEP answer causes handshake deadlock when viewer offers passive
test: tests/whep.test.js, describe 'WHEP answer a=setup matches the DTLS role given to mediasoup': "answers a=setup:active in every section for a <session|media>-level a=setup:passive offer, with remote role 'server'" (both failed before the fix); "reads the offered setup value case-insensitively (ABNF strings, RFC 5234 section 2.3)" (failed before); "takes one a=setup for every section from the section that supplies the DTLS parameters" (failed before); the actpass, active and no-setup cases (5 tests) passed before and after. Real-mediasoup check: results/check-17-dtls-probe.js.txt (output in results/check-17-probe-output.txt)
proof: The defect holds, though not by the mechanism the claim gives. lib/whep.js parseViewerDtls (line 195 at 109f819, the same at ac1c688) gives transport.connect() remote role 'server' for a=setup:passive, while buildActiveSection (line 531 at 109f819, line 373 at ac1c688) always wrote a=setup:passive. The claim says neither side then sends a ClientHello. That part is wrong: the probe (mediasoup 3.27.1 worker, WebRtcTransport connected as lib/whepRoutes.js does it, ICE completed with a hand-built STUN binding request) shows that for a passive offer mediasoup takes local role 'client' and sends a DTLS ClientHello (5 packets, with retransmits), and for actpass, active or no setup it takes 'server' and sends nothing. What is wrong is the answer. It said passive while mediasoup acted as client, and RFC 4145 section 4.1 allows only active (or holdconn) as the answer to a passive offer. A viewer that follows the answer also becomes DTLS client (two clients, no handshake); a strict one rejects the answer. Only a viewer that ignores the answer's setup worked. Browsers offer actpass (JSEP), so the case is non-browser WHEP clients that offer passive, which the code meant to support. The probe gave the same result on lib/whep.js from ac1c688, so the original code had the defect too. Before the fix, node --test --test-name-pattern=a=setup tests/whep.test.js: 4 of 9 new tests failed, e.g. expected setups ['active','active'], actual ['passive','passive'] with role 'server'. Fix: one helper, viewerDtlsRoles, gives both the remote role and the answer's a=setup (passive -> 'server'/active, anything else -> 'client'/passive), read case-insensitively from the video (else audio) section, one value for every answered section. After the fix the probe shows answer a=setup:active for the passive offer, matching mediasoup's client role, and the other answers unchanged. tests/whep.test.js 121/121; npm run lint, npm run typecheck pass; npm test 1060/1060. Commit a863cb6 on lane/netcheck.
